correctness.rationale: For each clockwise/anticlockwise neighbor transition rate gamma, rotated active signs are independent telegraphs flipping at gamma. The stationary coordinate density follows from the zero-flux telegraph Fokker–Planck equations. Generic projections are convolutions of independent symmetric Betas; four and only four corner collisions create the singularities. Local simplex and opposing-corner integrals give the two exact Beta coefficients, with convergence for 0<beta<1/2; Euler reflection yields their ratio. Two-sided inner and one-sided outer limits, beta=1/2 log transition, square-symmetry inversion, and beta>1/2 continuity were checked against exact mathematical conditions. Replayed CHECK.py passed 23 assertions; quadrature does not replace proof.

Searches of published-finding corpus, accessible published comparison titles/claims and primary text found no direct four-caustic statement. The source law implicitly contains the information, so a residual priority risk is retained.

value.rationale: The observable is physically motivated: an experiment may measure only a one-dimensional position projection while seeking persistence, propulsion length, and orientation relative to a discrete motor lattice. A generic projection unexpectedly creates four integrable singular peaks instead of the known three in the Cartesian section. Their universal Beta-amplitude ratio gives a strict closed-form inverse without measuring higher moments or accessing the full 2D distribution. The result is an exact nontrivial geometric/singularity classification of a natural physical model; the finite-data noise sensitivity remains outside the theorem.
